content: Wounds and injuries require both effective therapeutic interventions and robust strategies for prevention and control. The organization and administration of healthcare delivery systems, including emergency medical services, play a critical role in ensuring high standards of care. The World Health Organization (WHO), along with the Department of Violence and Injury Prevention and Disability, and international organizations such as the International Association for Trauma Surgery and Intensive Care (IATSIC) and the International Society of Surgery, have been instrumental in advancing global trauma care. Injuries are a significant public health issue, causing approximately 8 million deaths annually and leaving many more individuals disabled. The burden of injury is disproportionately high in lowand middle-income countries, where over 90% of injury-related deaths occur. High-income countries have successfully reduced trauma mortality rates by implementing well-organized trauma systems that address all aspects of care, from prehospital settings to hospital resuscitation and long-term definitive care. However, such systems are minimally implemented in lowand middle-income countries. To promote the global implementation of effective, affordable, and sustainable trauma systems, WHO and IATSIC have collaborated to develop guidelines for essential trauma care. These guidelines outline the core trauma care services that should be accessible to every injured person worldwide, even in the lowest-income settings. Since their release, these guidelines have catalyzed improvements in trauma systems in many countries. In response to a World Health Assembly resolution calling for strengthened trauma and emergency care services, WHO and IATSIC have expanded their collaborative efforts to produce a guideline on trauma quality improvement (QI). This document provides practical guidance to support the establishment of QI programs for trauma care, emphasizing basic methods applicable to all countries, regardless of economic status. The guidelines aim to stimulate the growth of QI programs globally and foster collaboration among those involved in trauma care and related patient safety initiatives. Quality improvement programs offer an affordable and sustainable means to enhance trauma care. By doing so, many preventable deaths among injury victims can be avoided. The guidelines provide detailed instructions on implementing QI programs, including morbidity and mortality (M&M) conferences and preventable death panel reviews, which are particularly relevant for strengthening trauma care in lowand middle-income countries. M&M conferences, already conducted in many hospitals worldwide, can be optimized to improve trauma care by focusing on detailed procedures, identifying system-related issues, and developing actionable corrective plans. Preventable death panel reviews offer formal input on the preventability of trauma deaths and identify areas of care that require improvement. These reviews involve multidisciplinary clinicians, whose expertise and investment in corrective actions enhance the success of these initiatives. Advanced QI techniques, such as using medical record systems to monitor specific variables (audit filters) and employing statistical methods for severity adjustment, are also discussed. Additionally, the guidelines address the importance of adequate data collection and management, which may involve establishing formal trauma registries in a cost-effective and sustainable manner. The guidelines conclude with a discussion on the appropriateness of different QI techniques at various levels of the healthcare system and their overlap with related activities, such as clinical algorithms for trauma care, patient safety efforts, and healthcare management strengthening. Case examples are provided to practice analyzing clinical data, identifying care problems, and developing effective corrective strategies. In summary, these guidelines offer practical, universally applicable methods for improving trauma care quality. They are relevant to healthcare institutions in all economic settings and aim to enhance the organization and planning of trauma care services. By implementing these recommendations, healthcare providers can strengthen trauma care quality and save the lives of many injured individuals.
